items.headline: Chile becomes the first country in the Americas to eliminate leprosy
items.summary: The Pan American Health Organization verified that Chile has eliminated leprosy as a public health problem, the first country in the Americas to reach that milestone. Health officials announced the certification at a regional meeting in Washington this week.
items.why_it_matters: It shows that a disease once considered incurable and stigmatizing can be driven out of a country through sustained public health work.

items.headline: Brazil becomes the world's most populous country to eliminate mother-to-child HIV transmission
items.summary: The Pan American Health Organization confirmed Brazil has eliminated mother-to-child transmission of HIV, making it the largest country in the world to reach that status. The achievement was formally recognized at a regional health meeting this week.
items.why_it_matters: It proves that universal access to testing and treatment during pregnancy can stop a major disease from passing to the next generation, even in a country of more than 200 million people.

items.headline: El Salvador becomes the first Central American country to eliminate trachoma
items.summary: The Pan American Health Organization validated that El Salvador has eliminated trachoma as a public health problem, a first for Central America. Trachoma is a bacterial eye infection that has historically been a leading cause of preventable blindness.
items.why_it_matters: It marks steady regional progress toward wiping out a preventable disease that still blinds people in poorer parts of the world.
